method_card.title: Angle Facts & Properties
method_card.content:
Angles on a straight line add up to \(180°\). Angles around a point add up to \(360°\). Vertically opposite angles are equal.

Angles in a triangle add up to \(180°\). Angles in a quadrilateral add up to \(360°\). The interior angle sum of an \(n\)-sided polygon is \((n-2) \times 180°\).

Parallel lines: Alternate angles (Z-angles) are equal. Co-interior angles (C-angles) add up to \(180°\). Corresponding angles (F-angles) are equal.
method_card.example:
Find angle \(x\): Two angles on a straight line are \(x\) and \(130°\).

\(x + 130 = 180\)

\(x = 50°\)

gold.hint: Corresponding angles are equal, so set the two expressions equal.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle of \(3x + 15\) and a corresponding angle of \(5x - 25\) are formed. Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: Corresponding angles (the F shape) are equal, so \(3x + 15 = 5x - 25\).

guided_steps.pre: Move the x terms to one side: 5x − 3x =
Move the numbers to the other side: 15 + 25 =
guided_steps.hint: Both numbers cross over and add.

misconceptions.message: Keep signs straight: 3x + 15 = 5x − 25 gives 2x = 40, so x = 20. Adding the x terms by mistake gives 8x = −40 and x = −5, which cannot be right.

gold.hint: Interior + exterior = 180, and interior is 5 lots of the exterior.
gold.display: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 5 times its exterior angle. How many sides does it have?

guided_steps.say: Interior + exterior = 180°, and here interior = 5 × exterior, so \(5e + e = 180\).

guided_steps.pre: Add the lots of e: 5e + e =

guided_steps.done: Exactly 5 times, so 12 sides is right.
guided_steps.hint: Interior should be 5 times the exterior.

misconceptions.message: Interior + exterior = 180, so 5e + e = 180 (six lots of e): e = 30° and 360 ÷ 30 = 12 sides. Using 5e = 180 forgets the exterior angle itself.

gold.hint: Collect the x terms and the numbers, then set the total to 720.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A hexagon has angles \(2x\), \(3x + 10\), \(x + 50\), \(130°\), \(150°\) and \(x + 30\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: A hexagon's angles add to (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°.

guided_steps.pre: Add the x terms: 2x + 3x + x + x =

guided_steps.done: All six angles then total 720°, so x = 50 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Rebuild an angle to test x.

gold.hint: Split 360° into 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts; b takes 3 of them.
gold.display: Angles \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are at a point. \(a : b : c = 2 : 3 : 4\). Find angle \(b\).

guided_steps.say: Angles at a point add to 360°. Split it in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4.

guided_steps.done: A full 360°, so b = 120° is right.
guided_steps.hint: All the parts should rebuild the full turn.

misconceptions.message: Angles at a point add to 360°, not 180°. One part = 360 ÷ 9 = 40°, so b = 3 × 40 = 120°.
b is the 3-part share: 3 × 40 = 120°. 160° is c, the 4-part share.

gold.hint: Split 180° into 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts; the largest takes 5.
gold.display: A triangle has angles in the ratio \(3 : 4 : 5\). What is the largest angle?

guided_steps.say: A triangle's angles add to 180°. Split it in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5.

misconceptions.message: A triangle's angles add to 180°, not 360°. One part = 180 ÷ 12 = 15°, largest = 5 × 15 = 75°.
The largest is the 5-part share: 5 × 15 = 75°. 45° is the smallest (3 parts).

bronze.hint: A straight line is 180°, so subtract the known angle from 180.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two angles on a straight line are \(x\) and \(110°\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: The two angles sit on a straight line, so together they make 180°.

guided_steps.pre: Write the total for a straight line:

guided_steps.done: Back to 180°, so x = 70° is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add your answer back to the known angle.

misconceptions.message: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so x = 180 − 110 = 70°. Adding them gives 290, far too big for one angle.

bronze.hint: Angles around a point add to 360°, so subtract both known angles from 360.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Three angles around a point are \(120°\), \(85°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: Angles that meet around a point make one full turn, 360°.

guided_steps.done: A full 360°, so x = 155° is right.
guided_steps.hint: All three should make a full turn.

misconceptions.message: Subtract BOTH known angles from a full turn: 360 − 120 − 85 = 155°. Taking away only one leaves 240.

bronze.hint: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so set 3x + 10 equal to 70.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two vertically opposite angles are \(3x + 10\) and \(70°\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: Vertically opposite angles (across the X) are equal, so \(3x + 10 = 70\).

guided_steps.done: That gives 70°, matching the opposite angle.

misconceptions.message: Setting 3x + 10 = 70 gives 3x = 60, then divide by 3: x = 20. 60 is the value of 3x, not x.

bronze.hint: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A triangle has angles \(40°\), \(75°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: The three angles inside any triangle add up to 180°.

misconceptions.message: Angles in a triangle add to 180°, not 360°. x = 180 − 40 − 75 = 65°.

bronze.hint: The exterior angles of a regular polygon share 360° equally.
bronze.display: Find the exterior angle of a regular hexagon.

guided_steps.say: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, shared equally when it is regular.

guided_steps.pre: Write the total of the exterior angles:

guided_steps.done: 120° is the interior angle, as expected for a regular hexagon.
guided_steps.hint: Interior and exterior make a straight line.

misconceptions.message: That is the interior angle. The exterior angle = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°.

bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A quadrilateral has angles \(90°\), \(80°\), \(110°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: The four angles inside a quadrilateral add up to 360°.

guided_steps.done: A full 360°, so x = 80° is right.

misconceptions.message: Subtract the total of the known angles from 360°: 360 − 280 = 80°. 280 is just the three added together.

bronze.hint: Add both angle expressions, set the total to 180, then solve.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two angles on a straight line are \(2x\) and \(3x + 30\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: The two angles sit on a straight line, so \(2x + 3x + 30 = 180\).

guided_steps.hint: Work out both angles and add.

misconceptions.message: A straight line is 180°, not 360°: 5x + 30 = 180, so 5x = 150 and x = 30.

bronze.hint: Interior angle sum is (5 − 2) × 180, then divide by 5.
bronze.display: Find the interior angle of a regular pentagon.

guided_steps.say: Interior angle sum of a pentagon = (5 − 2) × 180.

guided_steps.hint: Five equal angles should rebuild the sum.

misconceptions.message: That is the exterior angle (360 ÷ 5). The interior angle = 540 ÷ 5 = 108°.

silver.hint: The exterior angle equals the two opposite interior angles added together.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two angles in a triangle are \(55°\) and \(x\). The exterior angle at the third vertex is \(130°\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles not next to it: \(55 + x = 130\).

guided_steps.pre: The two far interior angles add to the exterior angle. Type that exterior angle:

guided_steps.hint: Interior and exterior sit on a straight line.

misconceptions.message: 50° is the third interior angle (180 − 130). The question wants x: 130 = 55 + x, so x = 75°.

silver.hint: Find the exterior angle first (180 − 156), then divide 360 by it.
silver.display: A regular polygon has an interior angle of \(156°\). How many sides does it have?

guided_steps.say: Work through the exterior angle: interior + exterior = 180°.

guided_steps.done: A full 360°, so 15 sides is right.
guided_steps.hint: The exterior angles should make a full turn.

misconceptions.message: 24° is the exterior angle. The number of sides = 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Lines AB and CD are parallel. Angle ABE = \(65°\). Angle BEF = \(x\). BEF and ABE are alternate angles. Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: Alternate angles (the Z shape) between parallel lines are equal.

guided_steps.pre: Angle ABE is given. Type it:
BEF is alternate to ABE, so x =

guided_steps.done: 115° is the supplementary angle, not x, confirming alternate angles stay equal.
guided_steps.hint: That is the C-angle, which we did NOT use.

misconceptions.message: Alternate angles are equal, so x = 65°. 115° would be a co-interior angle (180 − 65).

silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A co-interior angle is \(72°\). Find the other co-interior angle.

guided_steps.say: Co-interior angles (the C shape) between parallel lines add up to 180°.

guided_steps.pre: Write the total for co-interior angles:

misconceptions.message: Co-interior (C) angles add to 180°, they are not equal: 180 − 72 = 108°.

silver.hint: Add the angles, set the total to 540, then solve for x.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately The angles in a pentagon are \(x\), \(2x\), \(3x\), \(90°\) and \(120°\). Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: A pentagon's angles add to (5 − 2) × 180 = 540°.

guided_steps.hint: Work out the largest, then the total.

misconceptions.message: A pentagon's angles add to 540°, not 360°: 6x + 210 = 540, so 6x = 330 and x = 55.

silver.hint: Both equal angles are 50°, so subtract 100 from 180.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately An isosceles triangle has one angle of \(50°\). This is one of the equal angles. Find the other angle.

guided_steps.say: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles. Here 50° is one of the equal pair, so both are 50°.

misconceptions.message: Here 50° is one of the two equal base angles, so both are 50°. The third angle = 180 − 100 = 80°. Treating 50° as the odd one gives 65°.

silver.display: Find the sum of the interior angles of a nonagon (9 sides).

guided_steps.say: Interior angle sum = (n − 2) × 180, with n = 9 sides.

guided_steps.done: Still 1260°, so the answer is right.

misconceptions.message: Use (n − 2) × 180: (9 − 2) × 180 = 1260°. Multiplying by 9 forgets to subtract 2.
